review_type: single AI curator; complete final answer personally read; identity visible; original rubric

errors.quote: an effect interval that does not rule out the prespecified meaningful effect criterion
errors.issue: This compatibility gate can be passed by an extremely imprecise held-out estimate that includes zero, important harm and important benefit. Specify a validation precision/effect criterion that distinguishes supportive replication from merely failing to contradict a meaningful effect; a prespecified weak rule remains weak evidence.

errors.quote: design-respecting permutation or another demonstrably calibrated method would receive greater weight
errors.issue: Explicitly state the null targeted by the randomization test. Exact sharp-null inference is not automatically exact for a weak average-effect null with heterogeneous effects; do not prefer a permutation result solely because it respects allocation. The simulated calibration and actual-scheme caveat reduce this concern.

rationale: Very strong donor-level design, informative cluster size, biological-versus-sampling zero distinctions, hierarchical support, blocked resampling, full-pipeline null simulation and independent validation. The main deduction is the overly permissive held-out compatibility criterion; clarify randomization-null scope as well.
reference_guardrails: Personally read complete candidate answers, exact question/packet, full frozen reference and curator operational extension. Only original-round rubric applied; later 10/5 deductions remain inactive.

Independent treatment replication is at the assignment level; subsamples can improve donor measurement without creating assignments. Between-donor treatment regression is identifiable; saturated donor fixed indicators would instead absorb donor-constant treatment.
High ICC or loss of significance is not proof of a false effect. Small independent n limits precision and approximation robustness, not automatic invalidation of every prespecified model.
Equal-donor, observed-cell-weighted and nonlinear conditional coefficients can have different estimands. State normalization, link and standardization before comparing methods.

Ordinary bootstrap is not a null sample. Null simulations need explicit no-effect generation, parameter uncertainty and repeated datasets to assess false-positive frequency; a single permuted dataset is not an empirical FPR estimate.

Respect actual randomization restrictions and joint pair/block sampling. Sharp-null randomization exactness does not automatically transfer to all average-effect nulls. Report coarse attainable p resolution with few assignments.

Held-out prediction and confirmatory effect inference differ. A lack of external holdout limits validation but does not invalidate a prespecified calibrated treatment test. All data-dependent preprocessing must remain inside development folds.

Frozen reference corrections are disclosed; no actual data analysis or full primary-methods audit performed. The source packet does not specify a concrete assay, outcome distribution or numerical design values, so appropriate calibrated alternatives are accepted.
